column1: # rpm_parse_evr ground truth. Every expectation here was MEASURED by running the
# oracle's own Ruby, never hand-derived from reading the algorithm.
# Columns, tab separated, no quoting: input, epoch, version, release, arch.
# "NIL" is Ruby's nil, i.e. the field is ABSENT; an empty field is the empty
# string. compare_values treats those two differently, so the distinction is
# load-bearing and the table must be able to spell both. No real epoch, version,
# release or architecture is the literal string "NIL".
# The epoch rows exist because rpm_parse_evr normalises through Ruby's
# Integer(), which is not decimal parsing: "010" is octal 8, "08" is a parse
# failure and so becomes absent, and 0x/0b/0d/0o prefixes, underscore digit
# separators, surrounding whitespace, a sign and arbitrary precision are all
# accepted. A port that reaches for a plain base-10 atoi silently disagrees.
# Oracle: puppet-8.10.0 lib/puppet/util/rpm_compare.rb, byte-identical to the
# To add an input: append a row with any four placeholder columns, then
# regenerate. The regenerator reads the inputs back out of this file:
#   ruby -e 'module Puppet; module Util; end; end
